hints.title: Date Range and Amount Filters
hints.text: Filter Purchases to include records where time_stamp falls within [startDate, endDate] inclusive and amount is at least minAmount.

hints.title: Distinct User Deduplication
hints.text: Multiple qualifying transactions by the same user should only count once using distinct user deduplication.

hints.title: Stored Function Return
hints.text: Enclose the aggregate query in the scalar subquery returned by the stored function.

hints.title: MySQL Stored Function Definition
hints.text:
```sql
CREATE FUNCTION getUserIDs(startDate DATE, endDate DATE, minAmount INT) RETURNS INT
BEGIN
  RETURN (
      SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)
      FROM Purchases
      WHERE time_stamp BETWEEN startDate AND endDate
        AND amount >= minAmount
  );
END
```

variables: U: number of distinct qualifying users
complexity.notes: Filtering and aggregating user IDs scales linearly with purchase rows.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Failing to deduplicate user_id with DISTINCT overcounts users with multiple eligible transactions.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Distinct hash set uses temporary memory proportional to distinct eligible users.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate correctly formulates BETWEEN boundary filter and COUNT(DISTINCT user_id).

solutions.approach: PostgreSQL Stored Function with Filtered Count Distinct
Pandas Boolean Mask Filtering with Nunique
solutions.code:
import pandas as pd

def count_eligible_users(purchases: pd.DataFrame, startDate: str, endDate: str, minAmount: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    filtered = purchases[(purchases['time_stamp'] >= startDate) & 
                         (purchases['time_stamp'] <= endDate) & 
                         (purchases['amount'] >= minAmount)]
    user_count = filtered['user_id'].nunique()
    return pd.DataFrame({'user_cnt': [user_count]})
